title: They wanted to be seen.
paragraphs:
They wanted to be seen.
Jesus chose to kneel.
And that’s where everything breaks.

Because deep down… we don’t mind serving—
as long as someone notices.
As long as it leads somewhere.
As long as it earns us something.
But what happens when it doesn’t?

What happens when you give your best…
and nobody claps?

When you stay faithful…
and someone else gets the spotlight?

When you serve quietly…
and feel completely invisible?

That’s the moment Matthew 23:11 stops being a verse…
and starts becoming a mirror.
“The greatest among you shall be your servant.”

Not might be.
Not if recognized.
Not after promotion.
Shall be.

And suddenly, greatness doesn’t look like a stage.
It looks like a basin.

Water dripping.
Dust washing off.
The King… on His knees.
Do you feel that tension?

Because something inside us resists that.
Not loudly.
But quietly.

We obey… but we compare.
We serve… but we secretly measure.
We give… but we keep score in our hearts.
That’s the hidden place nobody talks about.

The silent pride that whispers,
“I deserve more than this.”
Let me ask you something that might sting a little…

When was the last time you served
without needing to be seen?

When was the last time you chose the lower place
without hoping it would lead to a higher one?
Be honest.
Because Jesus didn’t just teach humility—He embodied it.
Philippians 2:6–8 says that though He was in the form of God, He did not cling to His equality with God, but emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant… even to the point of death on a cross.
Read that again.

The One who deserved all glory…
chose the lowest position.

That’s not weakness.
That’s divine strength.
But here’s the AHA moment:

We don’t struggle to serve because it’s hard—
we struggle because it exposes who we think we are.

If you believe you deserve the throne,
the towel will always feel beneath you.
And that’s the real issue.

Not your schedule.
Not your opportunities.
Your identity.

Because pride doesn’t always shout.
Sometimes it whispers in disappointment.
In comparison.
In subtle resentment when others are elevated.
SPIRITUAL MIRROR:

If serving feels like losing,
you might still be building a kingdom where you are king.
This is where grace steps in.
Because the Gospel is not “try harder to be humble.”
The Gospel is this:

You were not just slightly prideful.
You were spiritually dead in sin (Ephesians 2:1).
Your heart naturally curved inward—self-exalting, self-protecting, self-centered.
But Jesus…
He didn’t wait for you to humble yourself perfectly.
He came down.

Lived the life you couldn’t live.
Died the death you deserved.
Rose again so you could be made new.

Not improved.
New.

And when you repent—truly turn from self-rule—
and place your faith in Christ alone, something supernatural happens:

You don’t just act humble.
You become a servant from the inside out.

Because now your identity is no longer “the one who must be seen,”
but “the one already fully known and loved in Christ.”
That changes everything.

Now you can serve without applause…
because heaven already sees you.

Now you can kneel without fear…
because Jesus already lifted you.

Now you can choose the lower place…
because your worth is no longer up for negotiation.
But let me say something that might confront religious comfort:

You can sing worship loudly on Sunday
and still reject the lifestyle of a servant on Monday.
And Jesus sees both.

This isn’t about church activity.
It’s about heart posture.

You are not called to build a name.
You are called to carry a cross.

You are not saved to be admired.
You are saved to become like Christ.

And Christ…
washed feet.
So today, this is your invitation.

Not to try harder.
But to surrender deeper.

Lay down the need to be noticed.
Release the silent scoreboard in your heart.
Repent of the pride that disguises itself as “I just want to matter.”
You already matter.

Enough for Jesus to kneel for you.
Enough for Jesus to bleed for you.
Enough for Jesus to rise and call you His own.
And if you’ve been tired… overlooked… unseen…
Heaven has not missed a single moment.
Luke 16:10 reminds us that whoever is faithful in little is faithful in much.
Nothing is wasted in the Kingdom.

Not one quiet act.
Not one unseen sacrifice.
Not one humble choice.
If this is hitting your heart… don’t ignore it.
Not hype. Real transformation.
Stay close.
Because next… we’re exposing the hidden cost of wanting to be first.
